title: Traffic-slice precision gate and automatic autorestore for quantized rollouts
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary:
Implement a traffic-slice based precision gating controller that validates FP8/INT8 calibration candidates during staged canary rollouts and performs automated, auditable autorestore to a verified baseline when accuracy regressions are detected. This ticket defines the controller design, acceptance criteria, monitoring signals, and the automation to perform partial/complete traffic reverts.

Motivation:
Current canary flows perform global checks and surface alerts but require manual intervention to revert quantized deployments when quality regressions are found. We need an automated, fine-grained safety net that: (1) isolates regression scope by traffic slice (customer, route, prompt cluster), (2) uses statistically robust tests at low traffic volumes, and (3) performs low-risk partial restores before escalating to full rollback. This reduces MTTR and avoids unnecessary broad rollbacks.

Design overview:
- Traffic slices: controller accepts logical slices (e.g., route, customer_tier, region, prompt_cluster) and monitors each independently. Canary config includes target slices and weighting schedule (example: 0.5% -> 5% -> 20% -> 50%).
- Validation harness: for each slice, run three validators in parallel: (A) golden prompt pass rate (predefined prompt suites with expected tokens/likelihood ranges), (B) live-distribution differential metrics (embedding drift, log-prob delta vs baseline), (C) client-visible regressions (error rate, timeouts, hallucination proxies). Validators report per-slice time-series.
- Statistical gating: use sequential probability ratio test (SPRT) with priors tuned for low-sample regimes to detect meaningful quality deltas with bounded false-positive rates. Complement with bootstrap-based confidence intervals for embedding cosine shifts.
- Action policy: policy levels mapped to thresholds: NOTICE (informational), HOLD (pause further traffic increases to that slice), DRAIN_PARTIAL (shift X% of slice to baseline model, see phased values below), FULL_RESTORE (route entire slice back to FP16 baseline). All actions are logged to audit trail + Console rollout events.
- Fallback targets: default fallback route is the most recent verified FP16/FP32 baseline pinned in rollout config. Secondary fallback options: narrower quant profile (e.g., INT8 -> mixed-fp8), or redirect to hosted remote inference if local quantized pool is out-of-spec.
- Safety features: manual override, cooldown windows, hysteresis to prevent oscillation, and exponential backoff for re-trying quantized candidates.

Operational flow (example):
1) Canary starts for model v2-quant (INT8): schedule: 0.5% for 60m, 5% for 120m, 20% for 180m.
2) Controller monitors per-slice validators. At 0.5% the SPRT flags embedding cosine shift p<0.01 for route /search for the last 30m.
3) Controller issues HOLD for that slice (blocks further percent increases). Notification posted to Slack and Console.
4) If drift persists and exceeds DRAIN_PARTIAL threshold, controller routes 75% of /search traffic to baseline and keeps 25% on quantized to collect more signal.
5) If additional checks fail within 30 minutes, controller executes FULL_RESTORE for that slice and triggers rollback runbook steps.

Rollout phases and thresholds (configurable per-release):
- Canary Phase 1 (smoke): <1% traffic, SPRT alpha=0.05, warn_threshold=1.5 sigma.
- Canary Phase 2 (validation): 5% traffic, SPRT alpha=0.01, hold_threshold=2.5 sigma.
- Canary Phase 3 (scale): >=20% traffic, hold_threshold=3.0 sigma, full_restore_threshold=4.0 sigma or sustained failure for 30m.

Acceptance criteria:
- Controller can independently monitor at least 6 slices concurrently and compute SPRT decisions with end-to-end latency < 10 minutes.
- Automated HOLD or DRAIN_PARTIAL actions trigger with explanatory audit events and a link to the offending metric/time window.
- Full restore (route swap) completes within 2 minutes of decision for slice sizes up to 50% traffic.
- False-positive automated restores under synthetic no-regression traffic <= 1% over 100 trial runs.
- Integration tests and canary runbooks exist: runbook pulled into Console runbook library and referenced from release flow.

Observability & dashboards:
- New Console view: "Quantization Gate" with per-slice time series (embedding cosine, log-prob delta, API error rate, latency p95), SPRT test statistic, and current policy state.
- Alerts: Pager for FULL_RESTORE only; Slack channel + ticket for HOLD/DRAIN_PARTIAL.
- Links: Draft dashboard: https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/quant-gate (placeholder), Aggregation query PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/observability/pull/314

Testing plan:
- Unit: SPRT library tests, synthetic embedding shift generators.
- Integration: Local canary harness that replays historical traffic (from s3://redwood-ci/quant-test-replays) with controllable drift injection.
- Staging: mirror 1% traffic to staging quant pool and exercise full automation with a test-only route that asserts no user-visible impact.
- Regression suite: nightly test that runs the canary decision engine against known-good quant profiles to validate FP rate.

Artifacts & links:
- Design doc (Confluence): https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ENG/pages/123456789/Traffic-Slice+Precision+Gate
- Proto spec (GitHub): https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/6321
- Observability PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/observability/pull/314
- Runbook: https://drive.redwood.ai/runbooks/quant-gate-runbook.md

Security & compliance notes:
- All automated restores must be logged with request IDs and admin actor set to "quant-gate-bot" for auditability.
- If customer data is used for golden prompt suites, ensure PII scrubbed and KMS keys referenced in config.

Open questions / trade-offs:
- SPRT vs Bayesian sequential tests: SPRT is simpler and faster on streaming data; Bayesian posterior checks could reduce false alarms but are more complex to calibrate. Recommend SPRT for initial rollout, revisit Bayesian approach after 1 quarter.
- How to choose prompt suites per-route: start with curated small suites (10-20 prompts) maintained by product owners; longer suites can be used for nightly regression.
- Fallback churn risk: aggressive partial draining reduces user impact but increases complexity of traffic steering. Default to conservative drain percentages (50-80%) until ops confidence increases.

Next steps / tasks:
- ENG: implement controller+SPRT library and Circuit Breaker API (owner: Liam)
- ENG: add telemetry hooks in runtime to emit per-request embedding summaries and log-prob deltas (owner: Sadaf Ahmad)
- PM: finalize slice taxonomy and per-route prompt suites (owner: Mateo Ruiz)
- DX: design Console panel and runbook UX (owner: Priya Singh)

Estimated effort: 5 engineering points (controller + tests) + 2 design points for Console work.

Release plan:
- Beta (internal) rollout week 1: enable on internal customers and staging traffic slice.
- Public canary (week 3): enable on non-critical customer routes with auto-notify.
- Gradual expansion (weeks 4–8): widen slices and tune thresholds.
